NOTE:  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION INFORMATION
  Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each Open Session agenda item are
  available on the City’s website under City Council Meeting Agendas at www.RollingHillsEstates.gov and
  during regular business hours in the office of the City Clerk.

  City Council meetings are conducted in a hybrid format, allowing members of the public to attend in
  person or remotely using the teleconference and/or videoconference information provided below.

  Remote Meeting Participation Information:
  Zoom Link:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81230087615?pwd=UEH27AumElOrSbrvK4zWDSM4Y4PmAf.1
  Meeting ID: 812 3008 7615
  Meeting Passcode: 052440
  Dial-In Number: (669) 900-6833

  Members of the public may observe and participate in the meeting in real time using the remote
  participation information listed above. Members of the public participating remotely by telephone or
  online will be provided the same opportunity to address the City Council as members of the public
  attending in person, consistent with applicable law.

  Public comment is welcome on any item during City Council consideration of the item. An opportunity is
  also provided for the public to comment on non-agenda items concerning City matters. Members of the
  public attending in person who wish to address the City Council are requested to complete a speaker card
  and provide it to the City Clerk. Members of the public attending remotely may use the “Raise Hand”
  feature or other instructions provided on the meeting platform to request to speak. Written public
  comments may be submitted to the City Clerk at cityclerk@rollinghillsestates.gov prior to the meeting.
  Written comments received before 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting will be provided to the City Council
  and made part of the administrative record, as appropriate.

  Persons requiring a disability-related accommodation or auxiliary aid or service to participate in the
  meeting, or persons requesting interpretation assistance, should contact the City Clerk’s Office as soon as
  possible prior to the meeting at (310) 377-1577 or cityclerk@rollinghillsestates.gov.

MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 8, 2026

1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

MAYOR ZERUNYAN called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m.

2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

Led by Los Angeles County Fire Department Acting Assistant Chief Wade Kelsey.

3.  ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan

City Council Members Absent:  Brown Schachter

City Staff Present:  City Manager Greg Grammer
  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Assistant City Attorney Steve McEwen
  Administrative Services Director Fernando Estrada
  City Clerk Lauren Pettit
  Assistant to the City Manager Jessica Slawson

4.  CEREMONIAL ITEMS

A.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER "NATIONAL PREPAREDNESS
  MONTH"

MAYOR ZERUNYAN presented the proclamation to Los Angeles County Fire Department
Acting Assistant Chief Kelsey and declared September 2026 as “National Preparedness
Month.”

B.  PROCLAMATION: DECLARING SEPTEMBER 15 - OCTOBER 15 "HISPANIC
  HERITAGE MONTH”

MAYOR ZERUNYAN declared September 15 – October15, 2026 as “Hispanic Heritage
Month.”

5.  CONSENT CALENDAR

The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of the City
Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by a member prior to the
roll call vote. (Items removed will be considered under New Business.)

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  STEGURA, TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS 5A-F AS FOLLOWS BY
  THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS

  APPROVED.

B.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS OF AUGUST 2026

  APPROVED WARRANTS 70091 THROUGH 70118 IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $518,320.78, WITH PROPER AUDIT.

C.  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MINUTES OF AUGUST 20, 2026

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
   REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

D.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF AUGUST 25, 2026

  REVIEWED AND APPROVED.

E.  SPECIAL EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MINUTES OF AUGUST 24, 2026

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  SBCCOG BOARD MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

6.  PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Public comment received from Merlin David, Development Director of the Palos Verdes
Peninsula Education Foundation, announcing the upcoming Toast on the Coast fundraising
event on September 26, 2026.

7.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

None.

8.  NEW BUSINESS

A.  ORDINANCE AMENDING AND RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 10.44
  REGARDING THE REGULATION OF BICYCLES, ELECTRIC BICYCLES AND
  OTHER MOTORIZED DEVICES, AND CHAPTER 10.46 REGARDING THE
  REGULATION OF WHEELED VEHICLES ON PUBLIC EQUESTRIAN PATHS AND
  TRAILS

  Recommendation: That the City Council introduce Ordinance No. 764 for a first
  reading, and bring it back for a second reading and adoption at the September 22,
  2026 City Council Meeting.

Assistant to the City Manager Slawson provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA expressed appreciation for staff’s work and support for
regulating the use of e-bikes in the community.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN supported updating the code to accommodate necessary trail access
for equestrian-related services, including veterinarians and hay deliveries.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF,
  TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  INTRODUCE ORDINANCE NO. 764 FOR A FIRST READING AND DIRECT
  STAFF TO BRING BACK FOR SECOND READING AND ADOPTION AT THE
  SEPTEMBER 22, 2026, CITY COUNCIL MEETING.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 764 by title.

B.  ADOPTION OF FY 2026-27 PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
   Recommendation: That the City Council approve a Publicly Available Pay Schedule
  for the 2026-27 fiscal year in accordance with California Public Employees'
  Retirement System (CalPERS) regulations.

Assistant City Manager Davis provided a staff report (as per the agenda material).

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF, TO
  APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVED A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE FOR THE 2026-27
  FISCAL YEAR IN ACCORDANCE WITH CALIFORNIA PUBLIC EMPLOYEES'
  RETIREMENT SYSTEM (CALPERS) REGULATIONS.

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

9.  OLD BUSINESS

None.

10.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

A.  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION OF ORDINANCE NO. 762 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING CHAPTER 2.12 OF THE ROLLING HILLS ESTATES MUNICIPAL
  CODE PERTAINING TO THE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES
  DIRECTOR

  Recommendation: That the City Council hold the second reading and adopt proposed
  Ordinance No. 762 amending and restating Municipal Code Chapter 2.12 (Office of
  Administrative Services Director).

Assistant City Attorney McEwen provided a staff report (as per the agenda material), noting
minor typographical errors in Ordinance No. 762 and recommended they be corrected as
clerical corrections.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
No public testimony was received.

  COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  SCHMITZ, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  ADOPTED PROPOSED ORDINANCE NO. 762 AMENDING AND
  RESTATING MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 2.12 (OFFICE OF
  ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES DIRECTOR).

  AYES:  Huff, Schmitz, Stegura, Zerunyan
  ABSENT:  Brown Schachter

City Clerk Pettit read Ordinance No. 762 by title.

11.  CITY COUNCIL / REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS

COUNCIL MEMBER STEGURA reported on attending the South Bay Cities Council of
Governments (SBCCOG) and Clean Power Alliance (CPA) Board meetings, noting that Clean
Power Alliance successfully implemented a new electronic voting platform to streamline voting
for its 37-member board.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHMITZ reported on attending the California Contract Cities
Association’s (CCCA) Legislative Committee meeting and noted that three legislative bills
remain on the Governor’s desk for consideration and that information was provided to cities

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
 regarding potential support or opposition letters. She also noted an upcoming special CCCA
meeting will be held to review and discuss the proposed budget prior to its consideration at the
end of the month.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF reminded the Council that the Cal Cities Annual Conference will
be held in Anaheim this year, with the Los Angeles County Division luncheon scheduled for
Wednesday, September 23.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN reported attending Southern California Association of Governments
(SCAG) and CCCA Board meetings, where discussions focused on the next Regional Housing
Needs Allocation (RHNA) cycle, housing methodology, and potential improvements to the
process. He also noted discussions regarding the public health and safety challenges
associated with homeless encampments.

12.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF asked staff to provide an update on the Palos Verdes Drive North
/ Dapplegray School Intersection Improvement Project. City Manager Grammer reported
ongoing performance challenges with the project contractor and indicated staff is working with
Willdan to get the project back on schedule. Traffic remains open in both directions, with a
protected pedestrian path maintained for school children and other users. Phase 1 construction
remains ongoing with no estimated completion date; City Manager Grammer noted that the
contract includes provisions addressing delays but emphasized that the priority is getting the
work completed.

13.  CLOSED SESSION

None.

14.  ADJOURNMENT

MAYOR ZERUNYAN extended warm wishes for a peaceful, healthy, and happy New Year
to those celebrating Rosh Hashanah. He then adjourned the meeting in remembrance of the
25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, honoring those who lost their lives, the bravery
of first responders, and all those impacted by the tragedy.

MAYOR ZERUNYAN adjourned the meeting at 7:36 p.m. to Tuesday, September 22, 2026,
at 7:00 p.m. for the purpose of a regular City Council meeting.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

  _____
Lauren Pettit, City Clerk  Frank V. Zerunyan, Mayor

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
SEPTEMBER 8, 2026
